title: Back off Bluetooth discovery retries while the adapter refuses them

leads.summary: A replacement default adapter can inherit an exhausted retry budget
leads.consequence: If A has reached attempts=8 and the Quickshell default adapter changes directly to enabled, non-discovering B while the panel remains open, the running binding never goes false: onRunningChanged cannot reset attempts. Subsequent ticks return without requesting discovery on healthy B until the user closes and reopens the panel or the state transitions through stopped. This makes newly available devices invisible (Panel.qml:123-145), even if B itself has never been asked to scan.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus lifecycle harness (no reset on direct adapter switch)

leads.summary: Keep #11260's discovery-paused guard when integrating its pairing changes
leads.consequence: The manual three-way merge conflicts exactly at running. If this PR's running expression is kept without #11260's !root.discoveryPausedForAction, #11260 sets discoveryPausedForAction=true and stops discovery before pair/connect, then this Timer immediately re-arms with triggeredOnStart=true and issues a new StartDiscovery while the outgoing action is queued or running. That defeats the other PR's explicitly stated pairing fix on adapters whose inquiry competes with connection paging. Retain both predicates on resolution.

leads.summary: Keep #7385's audio-aware and manual-stop guards on the retry Timer
leads.consequence: #7385 protects an active Bluetooth A2DP sink and allows a user to stop its forced scan for the panel session. Its retry running binding conflicts with this PR's binding. Choosing this PR's binding alone restores automatic scanning while Bluetooth audio is connected or the user stopped the one-time scan, the audio-interruption regression #7385 is explicitly intended to fix. Conjoin the audio predicates when resolving.

leads.summary: A radio which repeatedly powers off and back on gets a fresh eight-request budget on every flap
leads.consequence: Unlike a panel reopen, adapter.enabled can change without user action. When an unstable controller drops Powered=false and returns true while the panel remains open and discovering=false, running toggles false/true, resetting attempts to zero. Repeating this cycle avoids the intended per-open cap and immediately reissues StartDiscovery each time the controller returns. Bound the budget to a deliberate user restart or explicitly account for spontaneous radio state changes. The scenario is conditional, not a claim that it occurs on the reported hardware.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus minor point 2 (power flaps reset budget)

leads.summary: Three diverged open PRs implement conflicting retry budgets and cannot simply be combined
leads.consequence: #13466 implements 5 attempts to 8s; #10176 implements 3 attempts with running stopped at cap; #13622 implements 5 attempts with running stopped at cap. None is stacked on #13543 (compare API reports diverged). Local merge-file with each PR's own base produced conflict markers in the Timer, despite GitHub's MERGEABLE state against the common target base; selecting this PR's Timer unmodified makes #10176 and #13622's new source assertions for attempts <3/<5 fail. Choose one schedule and reconcile the other PRs' lifecycle tests rather than accepting competing caps.

leads.summary: The new discovery tests pass even if the repeating retry Timer becomes one-shot
leads.consequence: The tests call pure interval helpers and regex-match their usage, but do not assert the timer repeats. Changing only discoveryRetry's repeat:true to repeat:false makes the panel try at most twice (triggeredOnStart, then once after its interval) while the new test still reports all checks passed, including 'backs off discovery retries'. Add a Timer behavior check or at least assert repeat:true within retryTimer. This is a test-fidelity finding, not a claim the reviewed head itself has repeat:false.
leads.triage: factually verified by coordinator (sol run 20260929T014740Z-9d8c1779: 55 ok, 0 not ok with repeat:false); not published, pre-existing merge-base property not claimed by the new tests

leads.summary: The panel still claims it is scanning after the retry cap has stopped all discovery requests
leads.consequence: With an enabled adapter that keeps refusing StartDiscovery, attempts reaches 8 while adapter.discovering remains false. The retry Timer still runs but onTriggered returns forever, and the empty-state message nevertheless reads 'Scanning for devices…' indefinitely. There is no scan/retry control in this panel, so the user is not told to close and reopen for another attempt; the discovered section is also gated on discovering. Change the empty state to report the exhausted retry budget and offer or explain a recovery action.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus minor point 4 (accepted trade-off); not published

leads.summary: BlueZ already restarts a current client's discovery after ordinary controller scan timeout
leads.consequence: The comment says the retry is necessary because discovery 'can also time out on its own', but BlueZ 5.87 already schedules a fresh controller discovery after a Discovering=0 mgmt event if clients remain, at IDLE_DISCOV_TIMEOUT=5s; a failed internal restart gets another retry after 10s. The panel's new backoff does not govern or need to govern those internal retries. Keep the explanatory comment focused on rejected initial requests, distinguish stopping a D-Bus discovery session from BlueZ's internal scan restart. This does not negate the reported rejected StartDiscovery flood.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** No defects found; three other open PRs (#10176, #13466, #13622) fix the same retry Timer differently and conflict textually with this one and with each other.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified**

- In a headless QML run of the PR's `discoveryRetry` Timer (mock adapter that never starts discovering), requests go out at 0, 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 61 and 91 s, then stop. The Timer keeps firing every 30 s as a no-op after that. At the merge-base the Timer is a flat 1 s repeat with no limit (from the source).
- `onRunningChanged` resets `attempts` before the `triggeredOnStart` trigger, so each new episode starts again at one second.
- The new tests pass at the head, and the head tests fail against the merge-base code.
- The change merges cleanly with the current `quattro` tip.

**Optional notes**

1. **Optional test improvement:** the limit checks compare against `bluetooth.discoveryRetryLimit` itself, so setting it to 1 (no retries) or 1000 (effectively unbounded) still passes all 55 checks. A check of the full request schedule catches both (reproducer below).
2. **Optional comment and reset fix:** the counter also resets when the adapter is re-enabled or comes back after `null`, not only when discovery starts or the panel reopens. An adapter that keeps powering itself off and on gets a fresh budget each time it comes back: an immediate request, then up to 7 more. In the rare case where Quickshell switches the default adapter directly to another enabled, idle one (the first adapter is removed while a second exists), the count is not reset, so an exhausted budget carries over (time-scaled harness run). Naming these resets in the Timer comment would keep it accurate, and resetting `attempts` when `root.adapter` changes would cover the direct switch (not tested).
3. **Optional integration note:** #11260 and #7385 add conditions to the same `running:` binding and conflict with the new `onRunningChanged` line. Their conditions would also reset `attempts` when combined, so whichever lands second needs to keep both the other's condition and this counter when resolving the conflict.

</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: retry limit not pinned (passes at 235f9b93)</summary>

Reproduced at 235f9b93 with Node 26.7.0, from the repository root, on a scratch copy.

Change only the limit, then run the PR's test file:

```bash
sed -i 's/^var discoveryRetryLimit = 8$/var discoveryRetryLimit = 1/' shell/plugins/panels/bluetooth/Model.js
bash test/shell.d/bluetooth-test.sh; echo "exit $?"
```

Actual output (excerpt; all 55 checks pass, exit 0):

```
ok - bluetooth backs off discovery retries to a 30s ceiling
ok - bluetooth retries discovery after a second before any attempt
ok - bluetooth paces discovery retries by the attempts so far
ok - bluetooth starts retries over each time discovery is needed again
ok - bluetooth keeps retrying discovery below the limit
ok - bluetooth stops retrying discovery at the limit
ok - bluetooth stops asking a controller that keeps refusing discovery
...
ok - bluetooth install leaves AutoEnable at its default
exit 0
```

`discoveryRetryLimit = 1000` also passes every check. The limit checks compare against `bluetooth.discoveryRetryLimit` itself, so a limit of 1 (no retry at all) or 1000 (effectively unbounded at 30 s) still satisfies them.

A check in the file's own style that pins the schedule the description promises (placed with the other retry checks, before the "Quickshell only forwards" comment):

```js
// The whole schedule: eight requests, the last about a minute and a half in.
const requestTimes = []
for (let attempts = 0, t = 0; bluetooth.discoveryRetryAllowed(attempts); ) {
  requestTimes.push(t / 1000)
  attempts += 1
  t += bluetooth.discoveryRetryInterval(attempts)
}
assertDeepEqual(requestTimes, [0, 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 61, 91], 'bluetooth asks eight times over about a minute and a half, then stops')
```

Actual results:

- At 235f9b93 unchanged: `ok - bluetooth asks eight times over about a minute and a half, then stops`, exit 0.
- With `discoveryRetryLimit = 1`:

```
expected: [0,1,3,7,15,31,61,91]
actual:   [0]
not ok - bluetooth asks eight times over about a minute and a half, then stops
```

- With `discoveryRetryLimit = 1000`: also `not ok - bluetooth asks eight times over about a minute and a half, then stops` (the actual list runs past 91 in 30 s steps).

</details>
